igcse-0580-functions-notation.description: Read mapping diagrams and substitute numbers or expressions into a function rule.

sections.title: What makes a rule a function?
sections.label: Read the input and the output
sections.intro: A function takes each allowed input and gives exactly one output. A table row or an arrow records one input and its output.

blocks.html: In \(f(3)=5\), the input is \(3\) and its output is \(5\). The mapping \(f:x\mapsto 2x-1\) states the same rule as \(f(x)=2x-1\).

figure.alt: Arrows from inputs 1 and 3 both reach output 5. An arrow from input 4 reaches output 8.
figure.caption: Every input has one arrow. Different inputs can share an output.

blocks.title: Read a function table
blocks.prompt:
The table gives three values of \(f(x)\).

\(x\)\(f(x)\)
\(-2\)\(1\)
\(-1\)\(4\)
\(1\)\(10\)

Find \(f(-1)\).
blocks.solution:
Find the row whose input is \(-1\).

\(f(-1)=4\)
blocks.hint: Match the input exactly before reading across.

blocks.html: Several inputs can give the same output. One input with two different outputs fails the function rule.

blocks.title: Check whether each input has one output
blocks.prompt: Which set of ordered pairs gives a function of the first coordinate?
blocks.solution:
In each pair, the first coordinate is the input.

\(\{(3,9),(4,9),(5,11)\}\) lists each input once. Two different inputs sharing an output is allowed.
blocks.hint: Read the first coordinate of every pair.

blocks.html: Start a table lookup in the input column. Read across that row.

sections.title: How do I substitute a number into a function?
sections.label: Evaluate the rule
sections.intro: Function notation tells you what to put in the input position. The letter before the brackets names the rule.

blocks.html: Replace every \(x\) by the indicated input. For a negative input, keep brackets around it before finding powers.

blocks.title: Substitute a negative input
blocks.prompt:
The function \(g(x)=5 x^{2} + 7 x - 9\) is given.

Calculate \(g(-4)\). Give an exact value.
blocks.solution:
Replace every occurrence of \(x\) with \(-4\) before calculating.

\(g(-4)=5\times(-4)^2+7\times(-4)-9=43\)
blocks.hint: Keep a negative input in brackets when raising it to a power.

retry.feedback: Square the whole negative input inside brackets first.

blocks.html: \((-3)^2=9\) but \(-3^2=-9\). The brackets change which part is squared.

blocks.title: Evaluate a fractional rule
blocks.prompt:
The function \(g(x)=\frac{x}{6} + 7\) is given.

Calculate \(g(5)\). Give an exact value.
blocks.solution:
Replace every occurrence of \(x\) with \(5\) before calculating.

\(g(5)=\frac{5}{6}+7=\frac{47}{6}\)
blocks.hint: Divide the input by the denominator before adding the constant.

blocks.html: Write the substitution before using a calculator. Keep an exact fraction when the question asks for an exact value.

sections.title: What if the input is an expression or the output is given?
sections.label: Keep the input as a whole
sections.intro: The rule works on any allowed input. An algebraic input can occupy the same place as a number.

blocks.html: For \(h(x+2)\), replace each \(x\) by \((x+2)\). If the output is given, set the original rule equal to that value and solve.

blocks.title: Use an algebraic input
blocks.prompt:
The function is given by \(h:x\mapsto 7 - 7 x\).

Find \(h(x + 6)\). Give an expression in \(x\).
blocks.solution:
Here the entire expression \(x + 6\) takes the input position.

\(h(x + 6)=-7(x + 6)+7=- 7 x - 35\)
blocks.hint: Use brackets around the complete input.

blocks.html: \(h(x+2)\) applies the rule to \(x+2\). It usually has a different value from \(h(x)+2\).

blocks.title: Recover an input from the output
blocks.prompt:
The function \(m(x)=2 x - 8\) is given.

Find \(x\) when \(m(x)=-6\).
blocks.hint: Set the whole rule equal to the stated output.

blocks.html: Ask whether the question supplies an input or an output before writing the first calculation.

glossary.definition: A rule that gives each allowed input exactly one output.

revision.body:
Methods

CheckMethod
Read the input and the outputIn \(f(3)=5\), the input is \(3\) and its output is \(5\). The mapping \(f:x\mapsto 2x-1\) states the same rule as \(f(x)=2x-1\).
Evaluate the ruleReplace every \(x\) by the indicated input. For a negative input, keep brackets around it before finding powers.
Keep the input as a wholeFor \(h(x+2)\), replace each \(x\) by \((x+2)\). If the output is given, set the original rule equal to that value and solve.

Worked line

\(h(x)=4x-1\) gives \(h(-2)=4(-2)-1=-9\)

Check yourself

Given that rule, find \(h(x+3)\).

Answer \(4x+11\)
revision.checks:
• Several inputs can give the same output. One input with two different outputs fails the function rule.
  • \((-3)^2=9\) but \(-3^2=-9\). The brackets change which part is squared.
  • \(h(x+2)\) applies the rule to \(x+2\). It usually has a different value from \(h(x)+2\).
revision.examTip: Ask whether the question supplies an input or an output before writing the first calculation.

igcse-0580-functions-domain-range.description: Identify legal inputs and find the possible outputs of finite, linear and simple quadratic rules.

sections.title: Which values belong to the domain and range?
sections.label: Read inputs and possible outputs
sections.intro: The domain contains the allowed inputs. The range contains the outputs actually reached from those inputs.

blocks.html: For a finite domain, substitute every allowed input and write each distinct output only once. With an increasing linear rule, input order and output order agree.

blocks.title: Read a finite range
blocks.prompt:
The function \(f(x)=\left(x - 9\right)^{2} + 6\) is given.

Its domain is \(\{7,8,10,12\}\). State the range as a set.
blocks.solution:
\(x\)\(f(x)\)
\(7\)\(10\)
\(8\)\(7\)
\(10\)\(7\)
\(12\)\(15\)

Output \(7\) occurs twice. List it only once.

Range \(\{7,10,15\}\).
blocks.hint: Evaluate all four inputs and list each distinct output.

blocks.html: A range describes the function values. When using an inequality for the range, write it in terms of \(y\) or \(f(x)\).

blocks.title: Use the endpoints of a linear rule
blocks.prompt:
The function \(g(x)=4 x + 9\) is given. The domain is \(-10<x\le 6\).

State the range in terms of \(y\).
blocks.solution:
The rule increases as x increases.

The excluded lower output is \(-31\) and the included upper output is \(33\).

Range \(-31<y\le 33\).
blocks.hint: Evaluate both boundary inputs. Carry the inclusions to the corresponding outputs.

retry.feedback: The lower output may be reached at the opposite input endpoint. Check where equality is allowed.

blocks.html: Braces are useful for a list of discrete values. A range from one endpoint to another needs an interval or inequality.

sections.title: How do I find the range over an input interval?
sections.label: Locate every possible extreme
sections.intro: An increasing line puts its smallest outputs at its left boundary. A decreasing line reverses this order. A quadratic can reach an extreme inside the interval.

blocks.html: Calculate the two boundary outputs. For a quadratic, check its vertex when it lies within the interval. Include an extreme output if some permitted input attains it.

figure.alt: A parabola from input 0 to 3 has a minimum at (1,2), and ranges from output 2 to 6.
figure.caption: \(y=(x-1)^2+2,\ 0\le x\le3\). The marked values show why the minimum is reached at the vertex and the maximum at the right endpoint.

blocks.title: Use the endpoints of a linear rule
blocks.prompt:
The function \(g(x)=9 - 5 x\) is given. The domain is \(-2<x\le 7\).

State the range in terms of \(y\).
blocks.solution:
The rule decreases as x increases.

The included lower output is \(-26\) and the excluded upper output is \(19\).

Range \(-26\le y<19\).
blocks.hint: Evaluate both boundary inputs. Carry the inclusions to the corresponding outputs.

retry.feedback: The lower output may be reached at the opposite input endpoint. Check where equality is allowed.

blocks.html: An open boundary for the input can correspond to the upper or lower output boundary, depending on the rule.

blocks.title: Test the vertex as well as the boundaries
blocks.prompt:
The function \(q(x)=\left(x - 3\right)^{2} + 10\) is given. The domain is \(1\le x\le 6\).

State the range in terms of \(y\).
blocks.solution:
The square is zero at \(x=3\). This input is inside the domain.

The endpoint outputs are \(14\) and \(19\). The larger is attained.

Range \(10\le y\le 19\).
blocks.hint: The smallest output can occur inside the input interval.

blocks.html: An inclusive bound is written with \(\le\) or a square bracket. A strict bound uses \(<\) or a round bracket.

sections.title: Which values are allowed in the first place?
sections.label: Check where the rule is defined
sections.intro: Any stated restriction takes precedence. Real-valued fractions and square roots also have constraints from their operations.

blocks.html: Exclude a value that makes the denominator zero. Inside a square root, allow zero and positive values. A square root in a denominator must be strictly positive.

blocks.title: Identify the excluded denominator value
blocks.prompt:
The function \(r(x)=\frac{10}{x - 4}\) is given.

The domain contains all real inputs except one. State the excluded input.
blocks.solution:
The denominator is zero exactly when \(x-4=0\).

Exclude \(x=4\) from the domain.
blocks.hint: Find which input makes the denominator zero.

blocks.html: An expression can be zero. The problem is division by zero, which is undefined.

blocks.title: Set a lower bound for a square-root input
blocks.prompt:
The function \(s(x)=\sqrt{x - 8}\) is given.

State the real domain in terms of \(x\).
blocks.solution:
The number inside the square root must be at least zero.

\(x-8\ge 0\) gives \(x\ge 8\).
blocks.hint: Include the input that makes the radicand zero.

retry.feedback: At the boundary the square root is zero, which is a permitted output.

blocks.html: State the allowed variable clearly. A condition on \(x\) ordinarily describes the input domain.

glossary.definition: The set of outputs reached from the allowed inputs.
An endpoint of an interval, included when the condition allows equality.

Methods

CheckMethod
Read inputs and possible outputsFor a finite domain, substitute every allowed input and write each distinct output only once. With an increasing linear rule, input order and output order agree.
Locate every possible extremeCalculate the two boundary outputs. For a quadratic, check its vertex when it lies within the interval. Include an extreme output if some permitted input attains it.

Worked line

\(f(x)=x+2,\ 1<x\le4\) gives \(3<y\le6\)

Check yourself

What changes if the input 1 is also allowed?

Answer \(3\le y\le6\)

igcse-0580-functions-inverse-linear.description: Reverse linear rules, find an inverse expression and check that an inverse returns the original input.

sections.title: How do I undo the original rule?
sections.label: Undo the last operation first
sections.intro: An inverse function reverses the input and output of the original. Start by asking what the original rule does last.

blocks.html: If the forward rule multiplies by \(3\) and then adds \(5\), the reverse rule subtracts \(5\) and then divides by \(3\). A negative multiplier is still undone by division by that multiplier.

figure.alt: A forward arrow maps input 2 to output 11. A return arrow maps 11 back to 2.
figure.caption: The same pair is used in opposite order by the function and its inverse.

blocks.title: Reverse the linear operations
blocks.prompt:
The function \(f(x)=3 x - 8\) is given.

Find \(f^{-1}(x)\). Give an expression in \(x\).
blocks.solution:
Write \(y=3 x - 8\) and solve for the original input.

\(x=\frac{y + 8}{3}\)

Use x for the new input.

\(f^{-1}(x)=\frac{x + 8}{3}\)
blocks.hint: Undo the addition or subtraction before undoing the multiplication.

blocks.html: Undo the operations in reverse order. Subtracting after division generally produces a different function.

blocks.title: Reverse the linear operations
blocks.prompt:
The function \(f(x)=8 - 4 x\) is given.

Find \(f^{-1}(x)\). Give an expression in \(x\).
blocks.solution:
Write \(y=8 - 4 x\) and solve for the original input.

\(x=\frac{y - 8}{-4}\)

Use x for the new input.

\(f^{-1}(x)=\frac{x - 8}{-4}\)
blocks.hint: Undo the addition or subtraction before undoing the multiplication.

blocks.html: Test the reverse rule on a pair whose forward output you know.

sections.title: How can I find an inverse by rearranging?
sections.label: Make the original input the subject
sections.intro: Write the original rule as an equation for \(y\). The task is to recover the old \(x\) from known \(y\).

blocks.html: Rearrange to express the original \(x\) in terms of \(y\). Then write \(f^{-1}(x)\), with \(x\) as its new input letter.

blocks.title: Reverse the linear operations
blocks.prompt:
The function \(f(x)=\frac{x}{5} + \frac{8}{5}\) is given.

Find \(f^{-1}(x)\). Give an expression in \(x\).
blocks.solution:
Write \(y=\frac{x}{5} + \frac{8}{5}\) and solve for the original input.

\(x=\frac{y - \frac{8}{5}}{\frac{1}{5}}\)

Use x for the new input.

\(f^{-1}(x)=\frac{x - \frac{8}{5}}{\frac{1}{5}}\)
blocks.hint: Undo the addition or subtraction before undoing the multiplication.

blocks.html: On a rule divided by a constant, multiply both sides first. Keep the full numerator together.

blocks.title: Evaluate an inverse from a known pair
blocks.prompt:
The function \(f(x)=6 x - 8\) is given.

Calculate \(f^{-1}(28)\).
blocks.solution:
Find the original input that produced \(28\).

\(6 x - 8=28\)

\(x=6\)

The inverse returns this original input.
blocks.hint: Work backwards from the input of the inverse to the original input.

blocks.html: Equivalent forms such as \(\frac{x+5}{3}\) and \(\frac{x}{3}+\frac{5}{3}\) give the same linear inverse.

sections.title: How do I check that an inverse really reverses?
sections.label: Follow a pair back
sections.intro: An inverse sends each permitted output back to its original input.

blocks.html: If \(f(2)=11\), then \(f^{-1}(11)=2\). Applying one rule and then the other returns the starting input, provided the original pair is allowed.

blocks.title: Check the inverse round trip
blocks.prompt:
The function \(f(x)=7 x + 8\) is given.

Find \(f^{-1}(f(7))\).
blocks.hint: Keep the inside calculation first and undo it.

blocks.html: The superscript in \(f^{-1}\) means inverse function. The reciprocal \(\frac{1}{f(x)}\) divides 1 by one output.

blocks.title: Distinguish the inverse from plausible rules
blocks.prompt:
The function \(f(x)=- 3 x - 9\) is given.

Which expression is \(f^{-1}(x)\)?
blocks.solution:
\(y=- 3 x - 9\)

Add \(9\) to both sides, then divide by \(-3\).

\(f^{-1}(x)=- \frac{x}{3} - 3\)
blocks.hint: Both the sign of the multiplier and the constant affect the inverse.

blocks.html: Label the end of a backwards calculation with the inverse notation so its direction is clear.

examples.title: Reverse the linear operations
examples.question:

solution: Write \(y=7 x - 3\) and solve for the original input.

examples.title: Distinguish the inverse from plausible rules
examples.question:
The function \(f(x)=- 7 x - 4\) is given.

Which expression is \(f^{-1}(x)\)?

  1. \(x + \frac{4}{7}\)
  2. \(\frac{x}{7} + \frac{4}{7}\)
  3. \(- 7 x - 4\)
  4. \(- \frac{x}{7} - \frac{4}{7}\)
solution: Add \(4\) to both sides, then divide by \(-7\).

Use x for the new input.

extraPractice.hint: Undo the addition or subtraction before undoing the multiplication.

extraPractice.title: Evaluate an inverse from a known pair
extraPractice.prompt:
The function \(f(x)=3 x - 13\) is given.

Calculate \(f^{-1}(-1)\).
extraPractice.solution:
Find the original input that produced \(-1\).

\(3 x - 13=-1\)

\(x=4\)

The inverse returns this original input.
extraPractice.hint: Work backwards from the input of the inverse to the original input.

extraPractice.title: Check the inverse round trip
extraPractice.prompt:
The function \(f(x)=4 x + 13\) is given.

Find \(f^{-1}(f(5))\).
extraPractice.hint: Keep the inside calculation first and undo it.

extraPractice.title: Distinguish the inverse from plausible rules
extraPractice.prompt:
The function \(f(x)=- 5 x - 13\) is given.

Which expression is \(f^{-1}(x)\)?
extraPractice.solution:
\(y=- 5 x - 13\)

Add \(13\) to both sides, then divide by \(-5\).

\(f^{-1}(x)=- \frac{x}{5} - \frac{13}{5}\)
extraPractice.hint: Both the sign of the multiplier and the constant affect the inverse.

glossary.definition: The rule that recovers the original input from an output.
Operations that undo each other, such as multiplying and dividing by the same non-zero number.

revision.body:
Methods

CheckMethod
Undo the last operation firstIf the forward rule multiplies by \(3\) and then adds \(5\), the reverse rule subtracts \(5\) and then divides by \(3\). A negative multiplier is still undone by division by that multiplier.
Make the original input the subjectRearrange to express the original \(x\) in terms of \(y\). Then write \(f^{-1}(x)\), with \(x\) as its new input letter.
Follow a pair backIf \(f(2)=11\), then \(f^{-1}(11)=2\). Applying one rule and then the other returns the starting input, provided the original pair is allowed.

Worked line

\(f(x)=3x+5\) gives \(f^{-1}(x)=\frac{x-5}{3}\)

Check yourself

Find \(f^{-1}(17)\) for this rule.

Answer \(4\)
revision.checks:
• Undo the operations in reverse order. Subtracting after division generally produces a different function.
  • On a rule divided by a constant, multiply both sides first. Keep the full numerator together.
  • The superscript in \(f^{-1}\) means inverse function. The reciprocal \(\frac{1}{f(x)}\) divides 1 by one output.
revision.examTip: Label the end of a backwards calculation with the inverse notation so its direction is clear.

igcse-0580-functions-inverse-restriction.description: Choose a branch for a quadratic inverse, read the inverse domain and reverse a reciprocal rule.

sections.title: Why might a function have no inverse function?
sections.label: Check uniqueness on the way back
sections.intro: If different inputs share an output, the output alone cannot identify the original input.

blocks.html: A quadratic such as \(q(x)=(x-2)^2+1\) takes the same value for inputs equally far from \(2\). Restrict the domain to one side of the vertex to make the reverse unique.

figure.alt: A horizontal line meets a quadratic on two branches. Only the solid branch on and to the right of the vertex is allowed.
figure.caption: \(y=(x-2)^2+1\). With the left branch removed, each attained output has one original input.

blocks.title: Find a second input with the same image
blocks.prompt:
The function \(q(x)=\left(x - 3\right)^{2} + 6\) is given.

The input \(6\) maps to \(15\). Which other input maps to the same output?
blocks.solution:
The distance from \(3\) is \(3\) on each side of the vertex.

\(q(0)=q(6)=15\)

The unrestricted quadratic has no inverse function.
blocks.hint: Look at the same distance on the other side of the vertex.

blocks.html: A horizontal line crossing the graph twice shows two possible inputs. A single crossing in the allowed region identifies one input.

blocks.title: Select the branch allowed by the original domain
blocks.prompt:
The function \(q(x)=\left(x - 4\right)^{2} + 6\) is given. The domain is \(x\ge 4\).

Which expression is \(q^{-1}(x)\)?
blocks.solution:
\(y-6=(x-4)^2\)

The original input satisfies \(x\ge 4\). Use the non-negative branch for \(x-4\).

\(q^{-1}(x)=\sqrt{x - 6} + 4\)
blocks.hint: Every output of the inverse must satisfy the original input restriction.

blocks.html: Check that the proposed restriction stays on a single increasing or decreasing branch.

sections.title: Which sign belongs in the inverse?
sections.label: Use the original input restriction
sections.intro: Rearranging a quadratic often gives two algebraic candidates. The original domain tells you which candidate the inverse can return.

blocks.html: For \(y=(x-h)^2+k\), rearrange to \(x-h=\pm\sqrt{y-k}\). Retain the non-negative branch if \(x\ge h\), or the non-positive branch if \(x\le h\).

blocks.title: Select the branch allowed by the original domain
blocks.prompt:
The function \(q(x)=\left(x - 5\right)^{2} + 6\) is given. The domain is \(x\le 5\).

Which expression is \(q^{-1}(x)\)?
blocks.solution:
\(y-6=(x-5)^2\)

The original input satisfies \(x\le 5\). Use the non-positive branch for \(x-5\).

\(q^{-1}(x)=5 - \sqrt{x - 6}\)
blocks.hint: Every output of the inverse must satisfy the original input restriction.

blocks.html: Keep the original vertex when the domain includes it. The branches give the same boundary output at that point.

blocks.title: Evaluate a restricted inverse
blocks.prompt:
The function \(q(x)=\left(x - 6\right)^{2} + 6\) is given. The domain is \(x\ge 6\).

Find \(q^{-1}(10)\).
blocks.hint: Keep only the root on the given branch.

blocks.html: Substitute an allowed output above the minimum and check that the recovered input lies on the stated side.

sections.title: What are the allowable inputs of the inverse?
sections.label: Swap input and output sets
sections.intro: The inverse receives values from the range of the original. Its outputs lie in the original domain.

blocks.html: For a reciprocal rule, rearrange the equation and check the new denominator. For a restricted square, use the original range of outputs as the input interval of the inverse.

blocks.title: Invert a shifted reciprocal
blocks.prompt:
The function \(r(x)=6 + \frac{9}{x - 7}\) is given. Take \(x\ne 7\).

Find \(r^{-1}(x)\) as one fraction.
blocks.solution:
Write y for the original output.

\(y-6=\frac{9}{x-7}\)

\(x-7=\frac{9}{y-6}\)

\(r^{-1}(x)=\frac{7 x - 33}{x - 6}\)

The inverse cannot take \(x=6\).
blocks.hint: Subtract the outside constant before rearranging the fraction.

blocks.html: The excluded value of the original denominator and the excluded value of the inverse denominator can differ.

blocks.title: Swap the range and domain
blocks.prompt:
The function \(q(x)=\left(x - 8\right)^{2} + 6\) is given. Its domain is \(8\le x\le 12\).

State the domain of its inverse in terms of \(x\).
blocks.solution:
The original function increases on this restricted interval.

Its range runs from \(6\) to \(22\), including both ends.

Domain of the inverse \(6\le x\le 22\).
blocks.hint: Inputs to the inverse are outputs of the original rule.

blocks.html: Carry the endpoint inclusion or exclusion along when you swap the sets.

examples.title: Find a second input with the same image
examples.question:
The function \(q(x)=\left(x - 6\right)^{2} + 3\) is given.

The input \(8\) maps to \(7\). Which other input maps to the same output?

  1. \(4\)
  2. \(6\)
  3. \(8\)
  4. \(9\)

The unrestricted quadratic has no inverse function.

  3. \(\sqrt{x - 3} - 7\)
  4. \(\sqrt{x - 3} + 7\)

  2. \(- \sqrt{x - 3} - 8\)
  3. \(8 - \sqrt{x - 3}\)
  4. \(\sqrt{x - 3} + 8\)

examples.title: Evaluate a restricted inverse

examples.title: Invert a shifted reciprocal

The function \(q(x)=\left(x - 3\right)^{2} + 4\) is given. Its domain is \(3\le x\le 6\).

State the domain of its inverse in terms of \(x\).

Its range runs from \(4\) to \(13\), including both ends.

extraPractice.solution:

State the domain of its inverse in terms of \(x\).
extraPractice.solution:
The original function increases on this restricted interval.

Its range runs from \(9\) to \(13\), including both ends.

Domain of the inverse \(9\le x\le 13\).

glossary.definition: Different allowed inputs always produce different outputs.
One side of a quadratic graph when a restriction selects it.
The turning point of the quadratic graph.

Methods

Use the original input restrictionFor \(y=(x-h)^2+k\), rearrange to \(x-h=\pm\sqrt{y-k}\). Retain the non-negative branch if \(x\ge h\), or the non-positive branch if \(x\le h\).

igcse-0580-functions-composition.description: Use Cambridge composite notation, apply functions in the correct order and simplify the resulting expression.

sections.title: Which function acts first in a composite?
sections.label: Read the notation from the input outwards
sections.intro: A composite uses an output from one rule as the input to a second rule.

blocks.html: In Cambridge notation \(gf(x)=g(f(x))\). Work out \(f(x)\) first, then feed it into \(g\). In \(fg(x)\), start with \(g\).

figure.alt: Input 2 passes through f to become 7, then through g to become 9.
figure.caption: The output of the inner function becomes the input of the outer function.

blocks.title: Evaluate a composite value
blocks.hint: Start with the function nearest the input.

blocks.html: The functions are written from outermost to innermost. The calculation begins with the rule nearest to the input.

blocks.title: Evaluate a composite value
blocks.hint: Start with the function nearest the input.

blocks.html: Write the nested version with brackets before working on a composite with unfamiliar names.

sections.title: Can the first output be an expression or use the same rule?
sections.label: Track the intermediate output
sections.intro: In a repeated composite such as \(gg(x)\), the first output is fed back into the same rule.

blocks.html: For an algebraic input to an outer rule, replace every occurrence of its variable with the inner expression as a whole.

blocks.title: Evaluate a composite value
blocks.hint: Start with the function nearest the input.

blocks.html: \((2x-3)^2\) means square the whole bracket. Squaring each term separately would omit the cross term.

blocks.title: Compose an algebraic input
blocks.prompt:
Use \(f(x)=6 x - 7\) and \(g(x)=\left(x + 2\right)^{2} - 9\).

Find \(gf(x)\). Give an expression in \(x\).
blocks.solution:
Apply \(f\) to the input first.

\(f(x)=6 x - 7\)

\(gf(x)=g(6 x - 7)=\left(\left(6 x - 7\right) + 2\right)^{2} - 9\)

\(gf(x)=36 x^{2} - 60 x + 16\)
blocks.hint: Keep the inner expression in brackets before simplifying.

blocks.html: Leave the inner bracket visible in the first algebraic line. Expand only when it helps the requested form.

sections.title: How do I simplify a quadratic or a fractional composite?
sections.label: Use the form the question asks for
sections.intro: After substituting, the output expression has a form you can simplify. A single fraction needs one numerator and one denominator.

blocks.html: For \(g(x)=1+\frac{3}{x+2}\), substitute the inner rule into the denominator. Write 1 over that denominator before combining.

blocks.title: Compose an algebraic input
blocks.prompt:
Use \(f(x)=7 x - 7\) and \(g(x)=\left(x + 3\right)^{2} - 9\).

Find \(fg(x)\). Give an expression in \(x\).
blocks.solution:
Apply \(g\) to the input first.

\(g(x)=x \left(x + 6\right)\)

\(fg(x)=f(x \left(x + 6\right))=7 \left(x \left(x + 6\right)\right) - 7\)

\(fg(x)=7 x^{2} + 42 x - 7\)
blocks.hint: Keep the inner expression in brackets before simplifying.

blocks.html: The original denominator must stay non-zero. Regrouping the expression does not make a forbidden input valid.

blocks.title: Write a rational composite as one fraction
blocks.prompt:
Use \(f(x)=2 x - 8\) and \(g(x)=1 + \frac{9}{x + 4}\).

Find \(gf(x)\). Give your answer as a single fraction.
blocks.solution:
Apply \(f\) to the input first.

\(f(x)=2 x - 8\)

\(gf(x)=g(2 x - 8)=1 + \frac{9}{\left(2 x - 8\right) + 4}\)

\(gf(x)=\frac{2 x + 5}{2 x - 4}\)

The original second stage excludes \(-4\), so here \(x\ne 2\).
blocks.hint: Substitute the inner expression into the denominator and retain its restriction.

blocks.html: Check a simple allowed value using both the original two stages and your final formula.

examples.title: Compose an algebraic input
examples.question:
Use \(f(x)=3 x - 4\) and \(g(x)=\left(x + 5\right)^{2} - 3\).

Find \(gf(x)\). Give an expression in \(x\).

examples.title: Compose an algebraic input
examples.question:
Use \(f(x)=4 x - 4\) and \(g(x)=\left(x + 2\right)^{2} - 4\).

Find \(fg(x)\). Give an expression in \(x\).

examples.question:
Use \(f(x)=5 x - 4\) and \(g(x)=1 + \frac{4}{x + 3}\).

Find \(gf(x)\). Give your answer as a single fraction.
solution: The original second stage excludes \(-3\), so here \(x\ne \frac{1}{5}\).

Find \(gf(x)\). Give an expression in \(x\).
extraPractice.solution:

\(f(x)=4 x - 11\)

\(gf(x)=g(4 x - 11)=\left(\left(4 x - 11\right) + 4\right)^{2} - 14\)

\(gf(x)=16 x^{2} - 56 x + 35\)

Apply \(f\) to the input first.

\(f(x)=6 x - 11\)

\(gf(x)=g(6 x - 11)=1 + \frac{15}{\left(6 x - 11\right) + 2}\)

\(gf(x)=\frac{2 x + 2}{2 x - 3}\)

The original second stage excludes \(-2\), so here \(x\ne \frac{3}{2}\).

glossary.definition: A rule made by applying one function and then another.

revision.body:
Methods

CheckMethod
Read the notation from the input outwardsIn Cambridge notation \(gf(x)=g(f(x))\). Work out \(f(x)\) first, then feed it into \(g\). In \(fg(x)\), start with \(g\).
Track the intermediate outputFor an algebraic input to an outer rule, replace every occurrence of its variable with the inner expression as a whole.
Use the form the question asks forFor \(g(x)=1+\frac{3}{x+2}\), substitute the inner rule into the denominator. Write 1 over that denominator before combining.

igcse-0580-functions-combining-functions.description: Tell products from composites, use inverse pairs, and check inputs rolling through two stages.

sections.title: Which operation does this notation request?
sections.label: Tell nesting from multiplication
sections.intro: In the composite \(gf(x)\), the first output goes into the second rule. In the product \(g(x)f(x)\), there are two separate outputs at the same input.

blocks.html: For \(gf(2)\), find \(f(2)\) then apply \(g\) to that number. For \(g(2)f(2)\), calculate both at input 2 and multiply.

figure.alt: An input travels through the first machine. A gate before the second machine identifies a restricted intermediate value.
figure.caption: An input can pass the first rule and still fail the second rule.

blocks.title: Read the composite or product
blocks.prompt:
Use \(f(x)=3 x + 7\) and \(g(x)=\left(x - 3\right)^{2} + 8\).

Calculate \(gf(-3)\).
blocks.hint: A composite passes an output to the next rule. A product multiplies two separate outputs.

blocks.html: The symbolic strings look similar. Rewrite the composite with nested brackets when comparing them.

blocks.title: Read the composite or product
blocks.prompt:
Use \(f(x)=4 x + 7\) and \(g(x)=\left(x - 4\right)^{2} + 8\).

Calculate \(f(5)g(5)\).
blocks.hint: A composite passes an output to the next rule. A product multiplies two separate outputs.

blocks.html: When working on paper, write the intermediate output or the two separate outputs before the final line.

sections.title: How can I work backwards through a composite equation?
sections.label: Form the rule then solve
sections.intro: A function and its inverse undo each other wherever the associated input and output are allowed.

blocks.html: For a composite equation, write out the two-stage rule first. Solve the resulting equation, check the stated domain and substitute the retained answer.

blocks.title: Use an inverse in a composition
blocks.prompt:
The function \(f(x)=5 x + 7\) is given.

Find \(ff^{-1}(-5)\).
blocks.solution:
The inverse and original undo each other on allowed inputs.

\(f^{-1}(-5)=- \frac{12}{5}\)

\(f(- \frac{12}{5})=-5\)
blocks.hint: Work from the right. Apply the inverse first.

blocks.html: When a square gives two algebraic roots, do not report a root that is outside the domain in the question.

blocks.title: Solve a composite equation on a stated domain
blocks.prompt:
Use \(f(x)=6 x + 7\) and \(g(x)=\left(x - 19\right)^{2} + 9\).

Given \(x>2\), solve \(gf(x)=45\).
blocks.solution:
\(gf(x)=(6x-12)^2+9\)

\((6x-12)^2=36\)

Since \(x>2\), take the positive square root.

\(x=3\)
blocks.hint: Write out the composite and use the domain when choosing a square root.

retry.feedback: That algebraic root is outside the stated domain. Keep the root above the boundary.

blocks.html: A candidate still has to take the required value through both stages.

sections.title: Can this proposed input pass through both functions?
sections.label: Check the intermediate value
sections.intro: Both stages must be defined. A perfectly valid input for the first rule can give a value that the second rule cannot receive.

blocks.html: Use the first rule to find the intermediate value. For an outer fraction, test this value in its original denominator before simplifying.

blocks.title: Trace an input through a restricted second stage
blocks.prompt:
Use \(f(x)=7 x - 46\) and \(g(x)=\frac{9}{x - 3}\).

For which proposed input is \(gf(x)\) undefined?
blocks.solution:
The second function cannot receive \(3\).

\(f(7)=3\)

So the proposed input \(7\) gives a zero denominator in the second stage.
blocks.hint: The value that enters the denominator is an output of the first function.

blocks.html: Cancellation can remove a factor from the final formula. It does not fill the gap at an input that made the original expression undefined.

blocks.title: Keep the exclusion after cancelling
blocks.prompt:
Use \(f(x)=2 x + 8\) and \(g(x)=\frac{x^{2} - 16}{x-4}\), with \(x\ne 4\) for \(g\).

The rule for \(gf(x)\) simplifies to \(2 x + 12\). Which input must still be excluded?
blocks.solution:
Before cancelling, the denominator is \(f(x)-4\).

\(f(x)=2 x + 8=4\)

\(x=-2\)
blocks.hint: Check which original input makes the uncancelled denominator zero.

blocks.html: When the question gives an exclusion, carry it through the substitution before cancelling.

extraPractice.hint: A composite passes an output to the next rule. A product multiplies two separate outputs.

extraPractice.title: Use an inverse in a composition
extraPractice.prompt:
The function \(f(x)=3 x + 11\) is given.

Find \(ff^{-1}(-3)\).
extraPractice.solution:
The inverse and original undo each other on allowed inputs.

\(f^{-1}(-3)=- \frac{14}{3}\)

\(f(- \frac{14}{3})=-3\)
extraPractice.hint: Work from the right. Apply the inverse first.

extraPractice.title: Solve a composite equation on a stated domain
extraPractice.prompt:
Use \(f(x)=4 x + 11\) and \(g(x)=\left(x - 27\right)^{2} + 14\).

Given \(x>4\), solve \(gf(x)=30\).
extraPractice.solution:
\(gf(x)=(4x-16)^2+14\)

\((4x-16)^2=16\)

Since \(x>4\), take the positive square root.

\(x=5\)
extraPractice.hint: Write out the composite and use the domain when choosing a square root.

retry.feedback: That algebraic root is outside the stated domain. Keep the root above the boundary.

extraPractice.title: Trace an input through a restricted second stage
extraPractice.prompt:
Use \(f(x)=5 x - 50\) and \(g(x)=\frac{14}{x - 5}\).

For which proposed input is \(gf(x)\) undefined?
extraPractice.solution:
The second function cannot receive \(5\).

\(f(11)=5\)

So the proposed input \(11\) gives a zero denominator in the second stage.
extraPractice.hint: The value that enters the denominator is an output of the first function.

extraPractice.title: Keep the exclusion after cancelling
extraPractice.prompt:
Use \(f(x)=6 x + 11\) and \(g(x)=\frac{x^{2} - 4}{x-2}\), with \(x\ne 2\) for \(g\).

The rule for \(gf(x)\) simplifies to \(6 x + 13\). Which input must still be excluded?
extraPractice.solution:
Before cancelling, the denominator is \(f(x)-2\).

\(f(x)=6 x + 11=2\)

\(x=- \frac{3}{2}\)
extraPractice.hint: Check which original input makes the uncancelled denominator zero.

glossary.definition: The multiplication of the individual function values at a given input.
The first output before applying the second rule.
An input for which a required stage is undefined.

revision.body:
Methods

CheckMethod
Tell nesting from multiplicationFor \(gf(2)\), find \(f(2)\) then apply \(g\) to that number. For \(g(2)f(2)\), calculate both at input 2 and multiply.
Form the rule then solveFor a composite equation, write out the two-stage rule first. Solve the resulting equation, check the stated domain and substitute the retained answer.
Check the intermediate valueUse the first rule to find the intermediate value. For an outer fraction, test this value in its original denominator before simplifying.

Worked line

\(f(x)=x+2,\ g(x)=x^2\) gives \(gf(3)=25\) and \(g(3)f(3)=45\)

Check yourself

Using these rules, evaluate \(gf(1)\).

Answer \(9\)
revision.checks:
• The symbolic strings look similar. Rewrite the composite with nested brackets when comparing them.
  • When a square gives two algebraic roots, do not report a root that is outside the domain in the question.
  • Cancellation can remove a factor from the final formula. It does not fill the gap at an input that made the original expression undefined.
revision.examTip: When the question gives an exclusion, carry it through the substitution before cancelling.
